candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — Client Rights / Advocacy / access-to-care protections
candidate.educational_objective: Explain the core MHPAEA parity protection without incorrectly stating that the law itself requires every plan to offer mental health or substance use disorder coverage.

options.A: The plan must cover every possible mental health and substance use disorder service without utilization limits
options.B: Financial requirements and treatment limitations for mental health or substance use disorder benefits generally cannot be more restrictive than the applicable parity standard for medical/surgical benefits
options.C: Parity requires every health plan in the United States to add mental health and substance use disorder benefits even if the plan otherwise would not provide them
options.D: Parity means mental health benefits must use exactly the same clinicians and facilities as medical/surgical benefits

candidate.rationale: CMS explains that MHPAEA generally prevents plans and issuers that provide both medical/surgical and mental health or substance use disorder benefits from imposing financial requirements or treatment limitations on MH/SUD benefits that are more restrictive than the predominant requirements or limitations applying to substantially all medical/surgical benefits in the relevant classification. Therefore B is the best answer. MHPAEA itself does not require every plan to offer MH/SUD benefits, does not prohibit all utilization limits, and does not require the same clinicians or facilities for both benefit types.
candidate.source_claim_supported: When a plan provides both medical/surgical and MH/SUD benefits, MHPAEA generally requires parity in financial requirements and treatment limitations; MHPAEA itself does not require every plan to offer MH/SUD benefits.
candidate.source_document_title: The Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act (MHPAEA)
candidate.source_locator: Introduction; 2013 MHPAEA Regulations — financial requirements and treatment limitations cannot be more restrictive than the predominant requirements/limitations applying to substantially all medical/surgical benefits; MHPAEA does not require plans to provide MH/SUD benefits
candidate.stem: A client asks what federal mental health parity protections generally mean when a health plan provides both medical/surgical benefits and mental health or substance use disorder benefits. Which response by the nurse is accurate?
